input.command:
cat > diagnosis.json <<'EOF'
{"spec_element": "requires",
 "proof_obligation": "bridge",
 "diagnosis": "Exchanger's precondition is too weak: it allows x == |s| (x < |s| + 1), so t[x := s[y]] in the body and t[x] / s[x] in the ensures clause can be out of range. The precondition should be x < |s|, which all callers (Sorter, tests) satisfy."}
EOF
sed -i 's/x < (|s|) + 1 \&\& y < |s|/x < |s| \&\& y < |s|/' program.dfy && sed -n 7p program.dfy && dafny verify program.dfy

content.text:
`program.dfy` now verifies: 6 verified, 0 errors.

**Cause:** The precondition on `Exchanger` was too loose. It said `x < (|s|) + 1`, which allows `x == |s|`. With that value, `t[x := s[y]]` in the body (line 14) and `t[x]`/`s[x]` in the postcondition (line 10) index past the end of the sequence. Both counterexamples show this: `x == |s|`.

**Fix:** I changed line 7 to `requires 0 < |s| && x < |s| && y < |s|`. Every caller, in `Sorter` and the test methods, already meets the tighter condition, so nothing else needed to change.

**Extra cleanup:** After the fix, the proofs all passed but `dafny verify` still exited with code 2. The cause was two "deprecated style" warnings about trailing semicolons that were already in the file (the `ensures` on line 40 and the `invariant` on line 50). I removed those two semicolons, and the run now exits cleanly.

`diagnosis.json` was written before the first edit and records `spec_element: "requires"`, `proof_obligation: "bridge"`. "Bridge" is the closest of the three allowed labels. The error isn't really about loop entry, the loop body or loop exit: it's a precondition too weak to keep the indexing in bounds.
